sources.title: Vite Vitejs Improper Access Control Vulnerability
sources.snippet: Vite Vitejs: Vite Vitejs contains an improper access control vulnerability that exposes content of non-allowed files using ?inline&import or ?raw?import. Only apps explicitly exposing the Vite dev server to the network (using --host or server.host config option) are affected. Required action: Apply mitigations per vendor instructions, follow applicable BOD 22-01 guidance for cloud services, or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.
supports: CISA KEV identifies CVE-2025-31125 as exploited in the wild.

sources.title: Exploit Public-Facing Application
sources.snippet:
Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system to initially access a network. The weakness in the system can be a software bug, a temporary glitch, or a misconfiguration.

Exploited applications are often websites/web servers, but can also include databases (like SQL), standard services (like SMB or SSH), network device administration and management protocols (like SNMP and Smart Install), and any other system with Internet-accessible open sockets.(Citation: NVD CVE-2016-6662)(Citation: CIS Multiple SMB Vulnerabilities)(Citation: US-CERT TA18-106A Network Infrastructure Devices 2018)(Citation: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks)(Citation: NVD CVE-2014-7169) On ESXi infrastructure, adversaries may exploit exposed OpenSLP services; they may alternatively exploit exposed VMware vCenter servers.(Citation: Recorded Future ESXiArgs Ransomware 2023)(Citation: Ars Technica VMWare Code Execution Vulnerability 2021) Depending on the flaw being exploited, this may also involve [Exploitation for Stealth](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1211) or [Exploitation for Client Execution](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203).

If an application is hosted on cloud-based infrastructure and/or is containerized, then exploiting it may lead to compromise of the underlying instance or container. This can allow an adversary a path to access the cloud or container APIs (e.g., via the [Cloud Instance Metadata API](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005)), exploit container host access via [Escape to Host](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611), or take advantage of weak identity and access management policies.

Adversaries may also exploit edge network infrastructure and related appliances, specifically targeting devices that do not support robust host-based defenses.(Citation: Mandiant Fortinet Zero Day)(Citation: Wired Russia Cyberwar)

For websites and databases, the OWASP top 10 and CWE top 25 highlight the most common web-based vulnerabilities.(Citation: OWASP Top 10)(Citation: CWE top 25)
supports: Contextual mapping: the investigation terms are consistent with ATT&CK T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application).

sources.title: CVE-2026-112946: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: Vite is a frontend tooling framework for JavaScript. Prior to 6.4.4, 7.3.7, 8.1.6, 8.2.4, and 8.3.3, import analysis can record a root-relative browser URL in safeModulePaths instead of the cleaned resolved module identifier. On a network-accessible, non-Windows development server, an imported project file whose URL matches an absolute host path can authorize a later raw-filesystem request for that host file, provided server.fs.deny does not block it. The request can disclose the matching file outside the project root, but it does not allow arbitrary path traversal because the host path must correspond to a project-relative URL authorized by the application graph. This issue is fixed in versions 6.4.4, 7.3.7, 8.1.6, 8.2.4, and 8.3.3.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2026-112946 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2026-112950: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: Vitest is a Vite-native testing framework for JavaScript and TypeScript projects. From 4.1.11 until 4.1.12 and 5.0.3, isFileLoadingAllowed and the filesystem read interpret backslashes differently on Windows in packages/mocker/src/node/interceptorPlugin.ts. When a client can reach the Vite dev server on Windows and register a redirect mock containing backslash traversal, POSIX joining preserves a Windows backslash traversal that the later filesystem read interprets as a path separator, so the client can read a file outside server.fs.allow that the Vitest process can access. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.12 and 5.0.3.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2026-112950 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

Learn how remote attackers exploit @fs ... | Webpage excerpt: CVE-2025-30208 – Vite Arbitrary File Read via @fs Path Traversal Bypass CVE-2025-30208 – Vite Arbitrary File Read via @fs Path Traversal Bypass Discover CVE-2025-30208, a critical arbitrary file read vulnerability in the Vite development server. Learn how remote attackers exploit @fs URL handling to access sensitive files. CVE-2025-30208 is an arbitrary file read vulnerability in the Vite development server. This vulnerability allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to access arbitrary files on the server’s filesystem by abusing Vite’s @fs URL handling. Vulnerable Component: @fs path handler in the Vite Dev Server This issue affects applications running Vite in development mode, exposing sensitive server-side files if the dev server is accessible remotely. Vite supports special paths like /@fs/absolute/path to import files directly from the filesystem during development. Normally, Vite restricts access to files outside its allow list (i.e., project root).

sources.title: CVE-2025-30208: Vitejs Vite Information Disclosure Flaw
sources.snippet: UNTRUSTED WEB RESEARCH (not PCAP evidence). CVE-2025-30208 is an information disclosure vulnerability in Vitejs Vite. Learn about its impact, affected versions, and mitigation methods. | Webpage excerpt: [PARTIAL WEBPAGE: only first 150000 bytes examined] CVE-2025-30208: Vitejs Vite Information Disclosure Flaw CVE-2025-30208 is an information disclosure vulnerability in Vitejs Vite that allows attackers to bypass file access restrictions and read arbitrary files. This article covers technical details, affected versions, and patches. Vite, a widely deployed frontend development tooling provider, contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability in its development server. The @fs endpoint denies access to files outside the Vite serving allow list. Appending ?raw?? or ?import&raw?? to a request URL bypasses this restriction and returns arbitrary file contents to the browser. The bypass exists because trailing separators such as ? are stripped in severa Network-accessible Vite dev servers leak the contents of any file readable by the Node.js process, including source code, environment variables, and credentials. Vite versions prior to 6.2.3 on the 6.2.x branch Vite versions prior to 6.1.2, 6.0.12, and 5.4.15 on earlier 6.x and 5.x branches Vite versions prior to 4.5.10 on the 4.x branch
